overview.badSay: You spent {n} more than you earned. Most of it was {top}.

overview.nwD: needs account balances; no source sends them yet
overview.stripLabel: This month’s spending, each band a category, as wide as its share

transactions.sub: Every row from every source, with your review choices applied. Text from files is shown exactly as it arrived.
transactions.choiceKept: Your choice is kept apart from the imported row and survives a re-import of the same month.
transactions.fixInSourceBody: Rows from that source are corrected in the file and uploaded again. Only Mercado Pago rows can be changed here.

review.sub: Rows the importers weren’t sure about. Approve them or pick a better category; your totals move within seconds.

reasons.needs_review: No category, or a transfer that may be spending
reasons.possible_duplicate: Same amount, place and day as another row
reasons.bcv_rate: Converted at the official Venezuelan rate
reasons.summed: A month total, not single purchases

review.saveFailed: That change didn’t save. Nothing changed; try again.

imports.sub: Upload a file from each source. A new file for the same month replaces the old one, and you can undo it.

rules.mercadopago: The monthly release report as CSV. One month per file, up to 5 MiB.
rules.notion: The notes log exported as Markdown (.md). The whole log, up to 5 MiB.
rules.excel: A monthly budget whose name ends in the month and year, like budget_Sep_2026.xlsx. Up to 20 MiB.

imports.inUseYes: Yes, these are the rows you see
imports.skippedTitle: {n, plural, one {# row was skipped; the rest came in.} other {# rows were skipped; the rest came in.}}
imports.stalledBody: Repair finishes it from the file already uploaded. Nothing is lost.
imports.reading: Reading rows. Totals update about a minute after it finishes.
imports.undoBody: Brings back the rows from the file before this one for {p}.

errors.name: The file name needs the month and year, like budget_Jun_2026.xlsx.
errors.never: The file never arrived. It may have been over the 20 MiB limit.

refused.source: Choose where the file comes from first.
refused.empty: That file is empty. Choose the file again.
refused.name: That file doesn’t fit this source. Check the rule above the file button.
refused.tooLarge: That file is over the size limit for this source.
refused.paused: Imports are paused for a while. Nothing was sent; try again later.
refused.unavailable: Imports can’t start right now. Nothing was sent; try again in a minute.
refused.daily: You’ve made 10 imports today, the daily limit. Try again tomorrow.
refused.bytes: Your stored files are close to the 200 MiB limit. Erase your data to make room.
refused.running: Another import is still running. Wait for it to finish, then send this file.
refused.conflict: That import didn’t start. Nothing was sent; try again.

rates.sub: One rate per month turns pesos into dollars for the dollar view. Your records keep the original currency.
rates.rtFoot: Rates keep two decimals. Changing one updates that month’s dollar figures at once.
rates.saveFailed: That rate didn’t save. Nothing changed; try again.
rates.invalid: Use a number above 0 with at most two decimals, like 1,424.37.

data.sub: What Cuenta stores about you, where it lives, and how to take it out or remove it.
data.sTxD: every row from your files, with the original text
data.sFilesD: kept so an import can be undone or repaired
data.sChoicesD: categories and approvals for Mercado Pago rows
data.storedFoot: Everything is encrypted and kept in one cloud account, filed under your sign-in. Nobody else’s sign-in can read it.
data.exportBody: Download every transaction as a CSV file with your review choices applied. Text that looks like a spreadsheet formula is made safe first.
data.delBody: Removes every transaction, file, choice and rate. You can’t undo it from here. Export first if you want a copy.
data.delBackup: Backups keep deleted records for 35 days before they’re gone for good. A note that an erase happened, with its time, is kept so nothing deleted comes back.
data.deleting: Deleting {a, plural, one {# transaction} other {# transactions}} and {b, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}…
data.deletedBody: Imports reopen at 14:35, after background work finishes, so nothing deleted can come back.
data.eraseUnfinishedTitle: The erase may not have finished
data.eraseUnfinished: The server didn’t answer in time. Imports stay closed until the erase finishes, so finish it now.
data.eraseRunning: An import is still running. Wait until it ends, then delete again. Nothing was erased.
data.eraseFailed: We couldn’t start the erase. Nothing was erased; try again in a minute.
data.erasedNote: Imports open again about an hour after the erase, once background work finishes, so nothing deleted can come back.

states.errB: The server didn’t answer in time. Your data is safe.

common.footer: Sign out when you’re done; the session also ends after 30 idle minutes.

signUp.title: Create your account
signUp.lead: Bring your own files and see where your money goes. It takes about three minutes.
signUp.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. A short phrase works well.
signUp.privacyBody: Cuenta keeps the files you import and the rows inside them. Nobody else’s account can read yours. You can export or erase everything at any time.
signUp.accept: I have read the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy> and accept the <terms>terms</terms>.
signUp.proof: When you press the button, your browser runs a short check, a few seconds long, to keep automated sign-ups out. There is nothing to solve.
signUp.errWeak: That password is too short or too common. Use at least 12 characters and avoid common words.
signUp.errLimit: Too many sign-ups from this connection. Try again in an hour.
signUp.errBot: The check didn’t pass, so we haven’t created an account. Reload the page and try again, or write to {contact}.
signUp.errAccept: Tick the box to accept the privacy notice and the terms.
signUp.errRefused: We can’t create an account with this address right now.

confirm.title: Check your email
confirm.lead: We sent a 6-digit code to {email}. The account is created once you enter it.
confirm.spam: Nothing yet? Look in your spam folder first.
confirm.resent: We sent a new code. The old one no longer works.
confirm.resentWait: You can ask for another one in 30 seconds.
confirm.errWrong: That code doesn’t match. Check the digits and try again.
confirm.errExpired: This code has expired. Ask for a new one.
confirm.errLocked: Too many wrong codes. Start again in a few minutes.
confirm.errStart: This sign-up has expired. Start again.

setup.title: Set up your authenticator
setup.lead: Cuenta asks for a code from an authenticator app each time you sign in. It keeps your money private even if someone learns your password.
setup.required: You can’t see any money screen until this is done.
setup.step1: Open an authenticator app on your phone and scan this square.
setup.step2: Type the 6-digit code the app shows.
setup.cantScan: Can’t scan? Type this key instead:
setup.errWrong: That code didn’t work. Codes change every 30 seconds, so type the newest one.
setup.errExpired: Your setup timed out. Delete the Cuenta entry you just added in your authenticator app, then sign in again.
setup.qrAlt: QR code with your authenticator key

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.lead: Type your email and password. Your authenticator code comes next.
signIn.errWrong: That email and password don’t match. Check both and try again.
signIn.errExpired: Your sign-in timed out. Sign in again.
signIn.errLocked: Too many wrong codes. Sign in again.
signIn.passwordChanged: Your password was changed, and every session on every device was signed out. Sign in with your new password.

code.title: Enter your code
code.lead: Open your authenticator app and type the 6-digit code for Cuenta.
code.errWrong: That code didn’t work. Type the newest one from your app.

reset.title: Reset your password
reset.lead: Type your email. If there’s an account, we’ll send you a code.
reset.sentLead: If {email} has an account, a code is on its way. It can take a minute.

resetConfirm.title: Choose a new password
resetConfirm.lead: Type the code from your email and your new password. You’ll still need your authenticator code to sign in.
resetConfirm.errWrong: That code doesn’t match or has expired. Check your email, or ask for a new one.
resetConfirm.resent: If there’s an account, a new code is on its way. The old one no longer works.
resetConfirm.errLocked: Too many wrong codes. Ask for a new code and start again.
resetConfirm.errStart: This reset has expired. Start again.

lost.title: Lost your authenticator?
lost.lead: You can’t reset it on your own. That protects your money if someone else gets your password.
lost.step1: Write to {contact} from the email you signed up with.
lost.step2: Say that you lost your authenticator. Never send your password or a code.
lost.step3: We check it’s you and reset it. You set up a new one the next time you sign in.
lost.wait: Once we confirm it’s you, we wait 72 hours before the reset, so nobody else can do it quickly.
lost.proof: We reply to that address only, and ask two or three things only you would know, such as roughly when you signed up or which files you imported.
lost.after: After the reset, every session on every device ends.

consent.title: Your data, in plain words
consent.lead: We changed this page. Read it, then accept to keep using Cuenta. You can find it again any time under Your data.
consent.leadRead: This is what you agree to when you create an account. You accept it once, on the sign-up page.
consent.keep1: The files you import, and every row inside them with its original text.
consent.keep2: Your review choices and your dollar rates.
consent.keep3: Your email, and the date you accepted this page.
consent.where: In one cloud account, filed under your sign-in. No other account can read it.
consent.howLong: Until you erase it. After that, backups keep it for 35 days, then it’s gone for good.
consent.remove: Export or erase everything, or delete your account, at any time from Your data.
consent.accept: I have read the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy> and accept the <terms>terms</terms>.
consent.record: We record that you accepted, with the date and the version of this page.
consent.leadFirst: Read this, then accept to start using Cuenta.
consent.errChanged: This page changed while you were reading it. Read it again, then accept.

delete.reauthLead: To delete your account, sign in again. That stops anyone using a computer you left open.
delete.warnLead: This erases everything and closes your account. It can’t be undone from here.
delete.warn1: Every transaction, file, review choice and dollar rate.
delete.warn2: Your sign-in. To come back, you’d sign up again.
delete.backups: Backups keep your data for 35 days, then it’s gone for good. Export first if you want a copy.
delete.working: Erasing {tx} transactions and {files} files, then ending your sessions…
delete.stay: Stay on this page until it finishes.
delete.partialTitle: Your account is closed, but not everything is erased
delete.partialLead: Every session has ended and you can’t sign in. We couldn’t erase {left} transactions yet. We keep trying; you don’t need to do anything.
delete.partialHelp: Questions? Write to {contact} and quote the reference below.
delete.doneLead: You’re signed out on every device. Here’s what we removed.
delete.doneNote: This page is the only record. We can’t show it again.
delete.doneBackups: Backups keep it for 35 days, then it’s gone for good.
delete.running: An import is still running. Wait until it ends, then delete your account. Nothing was deleted.
delete.notStarted: Confirm it’s you first, then delete your account.
delete.unfinished: Erasing your data didn’t finish in time. You’re still signed in and nothing else changed. Finish deleting picks up where it stopped.
delete.workingPlain: Erasing your data, then ending your sessions…
delete.partialClosedLead: Every session has ended and you can’t sign in. A last step didn’t finish; we finish it within the hour. You don’t need to do anything.

tooMany.signIn: For your safety, sign-in is paused for this account. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
tooMany.signUp: Too many sign-ups came from this connection. Try again in an hour.
tooMany.code: Too many wrong codes. Wait {minutes} minutes, then type the newest code from your app.
tooMany.wait: Waiting is the only fix. Trying again sooner won’t help.

notFound.label: Not found
notFound.title: We can’t find that page
notFound.lead: The address may be old or mistyped. Your money is exactly where you left it.

idle.banner: You were signed out after 30 minutes without activity. Sign in to pick up where you left off.

auth.forbidden: This form didn’t come from this site, so we didn’t send it. Reload the page and try again.
auth.proofFailed: The automatic check didn’t pass. Reload the page and try again.
auth.limited: Too many tries from this connection. Try again in {minutes} minutes.
auth.invalid: Some of what you typed isn’t valid. Check it and try again.
auth.unavailable: Something went wrong on our side. Reload the page and try again.
auth.sessionEnded: Your session ended. Sign in again.
auth.consentNeeded: Accept the updated privacy notice and terms first.

ended.lead: Sign in again to pick up where you left off.

common.readOnly: This page is for reading. You accept it once, when you create your account. If it changes, Cuenta shows you the new version and asks again before any money screen opens.
common.testStage: This copy of Cuenta is a test stage, not the finished service. Anything stored here may be wiped at any time, so keep your own copy of your files.
common.contact: Write to {contact} from the email you signed up with.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: What Cuenta keeps about you, where it lives, how long we keep it, and how to remove it.
privacy.keepAccount: Your email address, and what the sign-in service needs to check your password and your authenticator code.
privacy.keepFiles: The files you import, and every row inside them with its original text.
privacy.keepChoices: Your review choices and your dollar rates.
privacy.keepConsent: Which version of this notice and of the terms you accepted, in which language, and when.
privacy.keepSession: While you’re signed in, a session on our server. Your browser holds only a random id for it in a cookie, and a second cookie with your language.
privacy.keepSecurity: Security records, such as sign-ins, failed tries and password resets, with your account id and the time. They never hold your email, password, codes or network address.
privacy.keepLimits: To slow down abuse, we count tries per email and per connection. The counters hold a scrambled code, not the email or the address, and expire within a day.
privacy.keepMonitoring: How pages load and any errors on the page, so we can keep the site working. This uses no cookies, no account id, and nothing after the ? in an address.
privacy.where: On Amazon Web Services (AWS), in the us-east-1 region in the United States, in Cuenta’s own cloud account. Your data is filed under your sign-in, and no other account can read it.
privacy.leavesEmail: Sign-up and reset codes reach you by email from the sign-in service.
privacy.leavesPwned: When you choose a password, our server asks the free Pwned Passwords service whether it has appeared in a known data breach. Only the first 5 characters of a scrambled form of the password (its SHA-1 hash) leave our server, never the password itself or your email.
privacy.leavesNone: Nothing you import is sent anywhere else.
privacy.howLongData: Your files, rows, review choices and rates: until you erase them or delete your account. After that, backups keep them for 35 days, then they’re gone for good.
privacy.howLongConsent: The record of what you accepted: until you delete your account. Erasing your data keeps it.
privacy.howLongSession: A session ends when you sign out, after 30 idle minutes, after 12 hours at most, or when you close the browser.
privacy.howLongSignUp: A sign-up that is never confirmed with the email code is removed after 24 hours.
privacy.howLongLogs: Security records and server logs: one month.
privacy.removeExport: See and export everything you imported, at any time, from Your data.
privacy.removeErase: Erase all your data from Your data. You type DELETE to confirm, and backups drop it after 35 days.
privacy.removeDelete: Delete your account from Your data. That erases your data, your sign-in and the record of what you accepted, and signs you out on every device.
privacy.removeAsk: For anything else about your data, write to {contact} from the email you signed up with.

terms.title: Terms
terms.lead: The rules for using Cuenta, in plain words.
terms.what: Cuenta shows where your money goes, from files you bring yourself. It reads those files and shows you your own figures.
terms.check: The figures come from your files. Check anything important against the original statement.
terms.notAdvice: It gives no investment or financial advice and picks no products for you.
terms.notMoney: It never moves money and never connects to a bank. You bring the files.
terms.accountOne: One account is for one person. Keep your password and your authenticator to yourself, and sign out when you’re done.
terms.accountOwn: Bring only your own files: Cuenta is for your own money.
terms.accountLost: If you lose your authenticator, you can’t reset it on your own. See <lost>Lost your authenticator?</lost>
terms.limits: To keep Cuenta working for everyone, it limits how many tries and requests come from one person or one connection. Past the limit, it asks you to wait before trying again.
terms.leave: You can delete your account at any time from Your data. The privacy notice says what is removed and when.
terms.changes: If the terms or the privacy notice change, Cuenta shows you the new version and asks you to accept it before any money screen opens. The version is at the top of each page.

limit.title: Too many requests
limit.label: Limit
limit.lead: {seconds, plural, one {You asked for more than one person can in a minute. Wait # second, then try again.} other {You asked for more than one person can in a minute. Wait # seconds, then try again.}}
limit.why: The limit keeps Cuenta quick for everyone. Nothing you saved is lost.
